related_quotes.quote: It's taking the warning and translating it into: 'what does it mean for me?'
related_quotes.speaker: Geoff Tooley
related_quotes.note: About interpreting warnings, not about linguistic translation.

related_quotes.quote: a major problem during the KZN flood disaster was lack of geographical literacy
related_quotes.speaker: Prof. Cathy Sutherland

related_quotes.quote: Most of the deaths were in the peri-urban areas on the periphery of the city, not in informal settlements.
Many Durban residents on social media have been complaining that eThekwini did not give them an early warning to prepare ahead of the floods.
related_quotes.note: Municipal alerts were directed to social media pages; first municipal Facebook mention on the morning of 11 April.

notes: Individually reported sites total ~67 of 435-459 deaths (~15%); the remaining deaths were not attributed to places in accessible sources. Counts include some 'missing, presumed dead' (KwaNdengezi, Mzinyathi, Nthungwane, Inanda). No official per-area death table from eThekwini/KZN CoGTA was found; News24 'Deadliest Storm' special, Bhekisisa and Witness pages returned 403. Amnesty International 'Flooded and Forgotten' (2025) PDF could not be parsed and may contain relevant evidence: https://www.amnesty.org/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/AFR5303692025ENGLISH.pdf. Other named affected areas with no per-place count found: Molweni, Osizweni, Durban North, Umbumbulu, KwaNcolosi, Ndwedwe, KwaMashu, Amanzimtoti, Chatsworth, Merebank. eThekwini metro overall: isiZulu 62.82, English 26.77, isiXhosa 3.91.

Tshakhuma (Vhembe, Limpopo) and Mkhuhlu (Bushbuckridge) were the most-damaged areas but no deaths found there. Sources quoted SAWS safety advice in English ('Do not cross rivers without first checking water levels') but nothing on warning language.

death_sites.count_note: FloodList: 'a vehicle was washed off a low-lying bridge on the MR01 ... a 28-year-old female ... was swept away'. FloodList lists the Umgeni municipality among responding areas, which conflicts; KwaDukuza location used. Road-crossing death: victim may not have lived in the place.

notes: Single death. An IOL/Post item reports a separate Nonoti River flash-flood death at a family gathering (breadwinner, 36) - possibly a second death for this storm; not added because FloodList total is 1 and age differs (36 vs 28). Victim identity/language not inferred.

death_sites.place: Waterways Retirement village, Tongaat (44 units collapsed, 40 evacuated) - affected, no deaths reported

dominant_language_across_sites: English (all named affected places are formal coastal suburbs - opposite of April 2022 death sites)
notes: No deaths located. FloodList May 2022 gives no death count; KZN govt statement of 23 May mentions none; allAfrica only says 'several people lost their lives' without places. The 'at least 2' figure remains unverified. SAWS issued a Level 10 'disruptive rainfall' warning; province urged residents 'to be on the alert and to stay at home if possible' - no language information. These affected sites are named because they were reported (evictions/damage in formal areas get coverage), which is itself a reporting bias; care centres housing April displaced were also hit but not named.
